claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure.
The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has only moderate strength and plasticity relative to industrial requirements.
The proposed intervention is approximately 8% cold rolling followed by a low-temperature anneal near 700°C.
Cold rolling followed by low-temperature annealing will refine the eutectic lamellar spacing.
The treatment will induce a beneficial phase adjustment or phase decomposition.
Cold rolling introduces a high dislocation density in this alloy.
Cold rolling refines the eutectic lamellar interfaces.
Annealing near 700°C for a short time will cause partial recrystallization without appreciable coarsening.
The processed alloy will have a heterogeneous ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure.
Lamellar, grain, and phase boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the alloy.
The refined duplex lamellar architecture can improve strength and ductility simultaneously rather than necessarily sacrificing ductility.
Improved phase-boundary characteristics will impede crack propagation.
The treatment will increase work-hardening rate.
The treatment will increase yield and fracture strengths while retaining or increasing ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The refined microstructure will improve room-temperature creep resistance by impeding dislocation movement.
The treatment will reduce local compositional heterogeneity and consequently improve corrosion resistance.
The treated alloy will remain effective during thermal cycling between room temperature and approximately 700°C.
The treated alloy will perform better than the starting alloy under sustained loading and in saline or industrial corrosive environments.
The refined microstructure will be thermally stable during long-term service.

contradictions.description: The treatment is called a 'single-step' or 'single intervention' but explicitly consists of two sequential processing operations: cold rolling and subsequent annealing.
